subject: ACME POC Trial - Integration Plan & Success Criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>, Tom Brooks <tom.brooks@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: ACME POC Trial - Integration Plan & Success Criteria

Hi Samantha & Tom —

Thanks again for a great discovery call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the 4-week POC/trial so we can align on success criteria and who owns what. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Summary of what we heard from ACME:
- Goal: Validate Redwood for near-real-time summarization + action extraction in ACME’s customer support flow (avg. 2,000 msgs/day; 95th pct latency target 250ms).
- Primary success criteria: 1) Latency SLO <= 250ms for 95th pct, 2) API integration completed for streaming transcripts, 3) Extraction accuracy >= 88% on your labeled set, 4) Token cost <= $0.0008 per processed message equivalent.

Proposed POC timeline (4 weeks):
- Week 0 (this week): Kickoff, share tech spec, grant test API keys, confirm firewall/IP allowlist.
- Week 1: Basic API integration (SDK or REST), ingest 1k test messages, validate connectivity & auth.
- Week 2: Enable streaming & tool-calling pipeline (webhook integration), run 1k live-sim tests.
- Week 3: Evaluation on labeled set, metric reporting, iterate prompt/templates.
- Week 4: Final validation, exec review, go/no-go decision.

Owners / Contacts:
- ACME: Samantha (Program Lead), Tom (Engineering).
- Redwood: Marissa (Project Lead / Commercial), Rishi (Sales Engineer / Integration lead), Vivek (Customer Success).

Requested deliverables from ACME this week:
1) Test account / API endpoint or sample transcript dataset (anonymized).
2) Firewall/IP and egress rules to allow test traffic (if needed).
3) Point of contact for backend engineer pairing session.

Technical collaboration notes (Rishi will follow with detailed integration doc):
- We recommend starting with our NodeJS SDK for quick dev iteration (example routes: /v1/generate for batch, /v1/stream for streaming tokens).
- For streaming transcripts we use WebSocket or SSE; if you prefer server-to-server webhooks we can support that via our tool-calling hooks.
- Auth model for trial: time-limited API key + environment flag (test).

Attachments: acme-poc-tech-specs.pdf (tech checklist), redwood-poc-success-criteria.xlsx.

Next step: Rishi + Tom to sync for a 30-min pairing session. Samantha — would Thursday 3/4 10am PT work?

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Hi Tom / Samantha —

Thanks for the quick reply. Per Marissa’s ask, attaching a short integration checklist and the recommended API routes for the POC. High-level notes below; see attachment (acme-poc-tech-specs.pdf) for code snippets.

Integration highlights:
- Quickstart (NodeJS / Python SDK): use the SDK to call /v1/generate for synchronous calls. Example: POST /v1/generate {model: "redwood-2-small", prompt: "..."}.
- Streaming: we offer server-to-server webhooks and a /v1/stream endpoint (SSE) if you want client streaming. For ACME please plan for webhooks: we will POST incremental tokens to your callback and include a completion event.
- Tool calling / action extraction: use the /v1/func-call endpoint to trigger structured outputs (JSON payload with function name + args). We’ll provide a schema for your extraction target.
- Test keys: I’ll provision a test API key valid for 30 days and send it after we confirm firewall rules.

Firewall/IPs: our infra team uses a small egress pool; I’ll include the CIDR blocks in a follow-up (should be < 10 IPs).

Pairing session agenda (30 min):
1) Quick runthrough of SDK sample (10m)
2) Webhook endpoint handshake & security (10m)
3) Verify sample run & logging access (10m)

Attaching: acme-poc-tech-specs.pdf

—Rishi
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

From: Tom Brooks <tom.brooks@acme.com>

Subject: Re: ACME POC Trial - Integration Plan & Success Criteria

Thanks Rishi — the checklist looks good. A couple of quick technical Qs we hit in the pairing:
1) For tool-calling: can the /v1/func-call return multiple candidate actions with confidence scores, or only a single best action? We’d like candidates to run a downstream rules engine.
2) For streaming via webhooks: do you include partial token timestamps so we can align events with our call transcripts?

Also — we pushed the anonymized labeled set to the shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cACME-POC (folder: labeled_set_2026_03).

Tom
Senior Eng Manager, ACME

Subject: Re: ACME POC Trial - Integration Plan & Success Criteria

Hey Tom — quick answers below and notes from pairing session (copied here so Marissa has timeline context):

1) /v1/func-call: We can return multiple candidate actions with confidence scores. Response payload will be an array of {action, args, score}. We’ll include example schema in the repo.
2) Webhooks & timestamps: yes — webhook events include partial-token timestamps (ISO8601) and message-offset metadata so you can align with your transcript timestamps.

Follow-ups I’ll do this afternoon:
- Share exact egress CIDRs for firewall allowlist.
- Provision test API key and post to secure HubSpot ticket (not in email).
- Upload a small Postman collection and SDK snippets to the shared Drive folder.

Preliminary metric capture plan (for Week 3 eval):
- Latency histogram (p50/p95/p99) for both generate and func-call routes.
- Extraction accuracy (precision/recall) on your labeled set.
- Token cost estimate based on sample traffic.

Next internal owner notes: Vivek — can you confirm we have CS capacity to run the Week 3 lab & metric dashboard?

—Rishi
